title: The Dinner Table Project
intro: Text 1 is a poster that encourages families to eat one meal a week without phones.

visual.text: Tonight, the only thing to pass around is the rice.
One evening a week. Everyone at the table. Every phone in the basket.
A family of four sits at a small dining table, laughing as they reach for the dishes. On a shelf behind them stands a rattan basket holding four phones.

When did you last hear how your sister’s day really went? Not a thumbs-up in the family chat — the whole story, with the funny voices. Meals are when families used to talk. Now we eat side by side and scroll alone. Pick one dinner this week and take it back.

visual.title: Try it this week
items: Choose a night when everyone is home
Put a basket by the door; phones go in before the food comes out
Everyone shares one good thing and one hard thing from the day
Whoever reaches for a phone first washes the dishes

visual.text: “The first ten minutes were awkward. Then my dad told a story about his school days that I had never heard in fifteen years.” — Farah, 15
Collect a free basket and a set of conversation cards from the residents’ corner at Block 77.

text2.intro: Text 2 is taken from a letter to a community newspaper written by a mother of three teenagers.
paragraphs: For months, dinner in our flat looked like a waiting room. Five of us sat at one table, and most nights the only sound was the tapping of thumbs on screens. I told myself the children were tired after school and needed to rest their minds. Then I realised I had not heard a single story about my son’s day in weeks.

That was when we tried a phone-free dinner on Fridays. The children groaned. My husband, I must admit, groaned loudest. But by the third Friday, my son was telling us about a science experiment that had gone badly wrong, and we laughed until the soup went cold. We have not managed every week. Still, Friday is now the night nobody wants to miss.

Look at the picture in Text 1. What does it show, and how does this support the message of the poster?

scheme.answer: It shows a family laughing together at dinner while their four phones sit in a basket on the shelf, which supports the message that putting phones away brings a family back to talking and enjoying the meal.
points: It shows a family laughing and reaching for the dishes while their four phones sit in a basket on the shelf behind them [1]
This supports the message that when phones are put away, a family talks and enjoys the meal together again [1]
